title: Exterior powers of sheaves of modules and determinant lines
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $\mathcal E$ a sheaf of $\mathcal O_X$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. For $n\geq0$, let $P_n(U)=\bigwedge^n_{\mathcal O_X(U)}\mathcal E(U)$, the module exterior power [def-weil-pbc-exterior-algebra]. Its restriction from $U$ to $V\subseteq U$ is the unique semilinear map sending $e_1\wedge\cdots\wedge e_n$ to $e_1|_V\wedge\cdots\wedge e_n|_V$; these maps satisfy the identity and composition laws. Define $\bigwedge^n\mathcal E$ as the sheafification of $P_n$. The wedge of local sections is their sectionwise wedge followed by the canonical map to sheafification. In degree zero this is canonically isomorphic to $\mathcal O_X$. If $\mathcal E$ is finite locally free of constant rank $r$ [def-amb-finite-locally-free-module], its determinant line is $\det(\mathcal E)=\bigwedge^r\mathcal E$, with the degree-zero identification giving $\det(0)=\mathcal O_X$.

proof.text: For each restriction U to V, form the O_X(U)-alternating map sending a tuple to the wedge of its restricted entries in the O_X(V)-exterior power, viewed by restriction of scalars as an O_X(U)-module. Additivity follows from the restriction map and the wedge being additive in each entry; scalar compatibility follows from PresheafOfModules.map_smul and wedge multilinearity; equal entries give zero. Apply Mathlib exteriorPower.alternatingMapLinearEquiv to extend it to the exterior power. The pure-wedge formula is alternatingMapLinearEquiv_apply_ιMulti, and linearMap_ext proves uniqueness.

The identity comparison map acts identically on every pure wedge, by the module-presheaf identity law. The composite comparison sends a pure wedge first to the wedge of the f-restrictions and then to the wedge of their g-restrictions, equal to restriction along the composite by PresheafOfModules.map_comp_apply. The uniqueness just established proves both restriction laws.

In degree zero use Mathlib exteriorPower.zeroEquiv on every open, sending the empty wedge to 1. The restriction formula and the fact that a ring restriction preserves 1 show naturality on pure wedges; linearMap_ext extends this to all elements. These equivalences give a presheaf isomorphism to the unit presheaf. Sheafify it and compose with the invertible counit at the unit sheaf. The sheafification adjunction sends this isomorphism back to the sectionwise zeroEquiv map, proving the required empty-wedge formula. Any other isomorphism with that formula has the same image under the adjunction, because pure wedges span and all Fin 0 tuples are equal; injectivity of the adjunction and Iso.ext prove uniqueness.
